text:
Marathon Petroleum dropped 2.5% today, extending a broader decline over the past two weeks (-14% total). The immediate driver appears to be weakness in the crude oil market itself—US oil fell to $82.24 per barrel, down from higher levels earlier in the month—which directly shrinks refinery margins and profit. Refineries are running at high capacity (95.7%), so there's little room to cut costs by reducing production, meaning lower oil prices flow straight through to earnings.

The collapse of climate talks at COP31, which failed to include commitments against fossil fuels, removes a near-term regulatory risk that had been hanging over energy stocks. That should theoretically be supportive, but it's been drowned out by the fundamental oil price weakness and the stock's sharp two-week sell-off, which suggests investors are pricing in a broader energy demand concern or macro pullback rather than reacting to any single headline.
